submitter_note: MLA Ron Wiebe, Grande Prairie-Wapiti (joint northern MLA proposal)
community: Buffalo Lake and Kikino Metis settlements, Whitefish Lake (White Fish Lake) reserve; Saddle Lake; Heart Lake, Beaver Lake; Bigstone Cree (Wabasca)
request: Move Buffalo Lake and Kikino Metis settlements and Whitefish Lake reserve from Fort McMurray-Lac La Biche to Athabasca-Barrhead-Westlock, and keep part of Saddle Lake in Athabasca-Barrhead-Westlock.
quote: we propose that Fort McMurray - Lac La Biche transfer the Buffalo Lake and Kikino Métis settlements, as well as the White Fish Lake Reserve, to the electoral district of Athabasca - Barrhead - Westlock
note: Joint northern-MLA proposal (Cyr, Dyck, Jean, Loewen, van Dijken, Wiebe, Williams, Yao). Also asks that 'some portion of the Saddle Lake Reserve' remain in Athabasca-Barrhead-Westlock ("We believe the sections of St Paul County should remain in Athabasca - Barrhead - Westlock as should some portion of the Saddle Lake Reserve"), and that Fort McMurray-Lac La Biche keep Heart Lake and Beaver Lake reserves; objects that interim Peace River put Wabasca/Bigstone Cree reserve where MLA must leave district to reach it; wants Lesser Slave Lake district kept for its reserves and settlements. Submitter is an MLA, not a nation. Also adds a Sexsmith request for Grande Prairie-Wapiti.

'Bearspaw' is the Rocky View County community, not Bearspaw First Nation.

community: Tall Cree reserves; Garden River First Nation; Sucker Creek First Nation; Saddle Lake Cree Nation; Smoky Lake County Metis settlements; Blood Reservation; Siksika reservation; Wabasca
request: Move the Tall Cree reserves out of the Mackenzie/High Level riding into a Lesser Slave Lake successor (Peace River-Wabasca) to raise its Indigenous share, and place other reserves in specific ridings of his alternative map.
quote: since this riding was given this protection in the past due to its high proportion of indigenous people, I thought we can make a couple of further tweaks to boost that. The first is the already discussed of the Tall Cree reserves from Mackenzie county
note: Mapmaker's placements, mostly for population/geometry: Garden River FN with High Level-Grimshaw (p.82: 'we cannot forget to incorporate the Garden River first nation'); Tall Cree to Peace River-Wabasca (pp.82, 84; the only one justified by Indigenous representation); Sucker Creek FN with Slave Lake-Westlock-Barrhead (p.99); Saddle Lake Cree Nation in Morinville-Athabasca with 'Smoky Lake County without the Metis settlements' (p.99, settlements' destination not stated); Blood Reservation with Cardston County and County of Warner in Coaldale-Cardston (pp.101-102); Siksika reservation with Newell and Vulcan counties in Brooks-Vulcan (p.102). Names 'Wabasca Reservation' in riding name. No nation-voice; no request from any nation.

submitter_note: Jennifer Churchill, Executive Director, Alberta North Central Alliance (five First Nations and five municipalities)
community: Sawridge First Nation and the other Lesser Slave Lake nations (Swan River, Driftpile Cree Nation, Kapawe'no, Sucker Creek); Gift Lake, Peavine, East Prairie Metis settlements; Bigstone Cree
request: Keep the Lesser Slave Lake riding and do not separate Sawridge First Nation from the other lakeshore nations (historically one band, Kinosayo's Band).
quote: It also separates Sawridge First Nation from the other Nation’s along the lakeshore
note: Submitter is a joint First Nation-municipal alliance, not a nation alone; coded nation_or_council because it speaks for five First Nation governments (chiefs of Sawridge, Swan River, Driftpile, Sucker Creek and a Bigstone councillor are cc'd, p.133). Also objects that interim Mackenzie groups Indigenous communities from Lesser Slave Lake to NWT border (Driftpile resident with MLA in Zama City, p.131), that the split weakens the Lesser Slave Lake Indian Regional Council (p.132), and asks 15(2) status for its riding. Also: 'before the signing of Treaty 8 in 1899, the Nations along the south end of the Lesser Slave Lake were one Nation' (p.132).
